fields.meta_description: Build a podcast application form that collects guest pitches, links to past interviews, and recording setup, then sends each pitch to your host.
fields.h1: Build a Podcast Application Form for Guests and Co-Hosts
fields.hero_description: Build a podcast application form that keeps each guest's pitch and audio sample in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Host Needs Before Saying Yes to a Guest
fields.features_subheading: A podcast application form built in Emergent asks up front what you would otherwise chase over email before booking a recording.
fields.feature_1:
A topic pitch with a word limit

Ask for the episode topic in 150 words or fewer, plus three questions the guest would like to hear. The host reads the pitch and the questions together on one review screen.
fields.feature_2:
Past interviews and audio clips on file

Let guests link episodes they have appeared on, or upload a short audio clip if they have none. The links and files stay on the application, so nobody digs through an inbox.
fields.feature_3:
Setup questions that change the next step

Ask which microphone the guest records on and whether they wear headphones. Picking a laptop mic can send your producer a note to mail a loaner before the recording date.
fields.feature_4:
Pitches sent to the person who books

Route guest pitches to the host in Slack and co-host auditions to the producer by email. Name a backup reviewer for the weeks when the host is away at a trade conference.
fields.feature_5:
A recording release signed in the form

Close with your release terms in plain words and a typed or drawn signature. The signature and the date it was signed are saved with the application, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Code a developer can keep building

On paid plans, export the code for the form and its review screens to your GitHub repository. A developer can host it on your own servers or keep extending it from there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Shows Act on an Application
fields.tab_content_1:
Henrike reads every pitch with past interviews in Slack

Workbench Hours books one woodworking guest for each weekly episode. Anand Kandasamy pitches an episode on hand-cut dovetails and links 2 past interviews. Every pitch with past interviews goes to Henrike Osterlund, the host, in Slack, and she reads his the day he applies.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any guest on a laptop mic gets a loaner

The Long Haul Hour records truck drivers remotely, so its form asks what each guest will speak into. Cormac Ellery answers Laptop mic. Any guest on a laptop mic sets off an email to Matteo Quiroga, the producer, to ship a loaner before the March 18 recording.
fields.tab_content_3:
Samples rated 4 or higher get a callback

Old Ferry Road needs a co-host for its local history show, and every applicant uploads a 2-minute audio sample. Yewande Balogun, the producer, rates each one from 1 to 5. Sunniva Brekke's sample gets a 5, and every sample rated 4 or higher goes on the callback list.
fields.tab_content_4:
Ignatius books Philippa with her release on file

Pocket Garden Radio closes its guest form with a recording release: the episode's audio and video may be published and clipped for social posts. Philippa Okonjo signs it with a drawn signature. Ignatius Borrero, the host, books her with the signed release and its date on file.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Podcast Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a podcast application form that separates guests from co-hosts and puts each pitch in front of the right reader.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Offer the slots you record in
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose whether the form takes guest pitches, co-host auditions, or both. A guest applies for one episode, while a co-host applies for months of weekly recordings. One form can serve both by branching on its first question.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the topic of the episode, then ask what angle the guest brings that your listeners have not heard yet. Cap the pitch at a length you can read in a minute. Short pitches are easier to compare side by side.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a question about the microphone and one about the room the guest will record in. A laptop mic in a kitchen can be fixed before the date with a loaner or a quieter room. After the recording, it cannot.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Show only the days and times you record, such as Tuesday and Thursday mornings, and ask for the guest's time zone. An approved guest then picks a slot you can keep, with no email thread to settle the date.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the person who reads guest pitches and the one who scores co-host samples, and how each hears about a new application. Decide how quickly a pitch gets an answer, and who writes the reply to the guests you turn down.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste your questions and routing into one prompt, along with the release wording. Emergent builds the form, its review screen, and the table where every application lands. To change a question later, ask for the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test application that answers Laptop mic and links one past interview. Confirm the pitch reaches its reader and the loaner request goes out. Then open the table and check that the release signature was saved with a date.

faq_plan.q: What is a podcast application form?
faq_plan.a: A podcast application form is how a show takes requests to appear on it, whether from a guest pitching one episode or someone applying to co-host. It gathers the pitch, links to past appearances, and recording details in one place. The host can then decide on a guest without piecing it together from emails.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a podcast application form?
faq_plan.a: Decide who applies, what each applicant has to send, and who reads each application. Describe all of that to Emergent's AI form builder in a single prompt. It builds the form and the database that stores every application, and you can rename or reorder questions afterward by asking.

faq_plan.q: What should a podcast application form ask guests besides the topic?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a two-sentence bio the host can read aloud as the introduction, and how the guest pronounces their name. Add the one link they want mentioned at the end of the episode. Those three answers save a pre-call and spare the host a stumble on the guest's name in the first minute.

faq_plan.q: Should a podcast application form ask co-hosts different questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A guest commits to one conversation, while a co-host commits to a standing slot for months. Ask about weekly availability over the next 3 months and how they would split research and editing. Then ask why they want the seat. That makes it closer to a coaching application form than a guest pitch, since commitment and fit matter more than a single idea.

faq_plan.q: How do I screen guests who apply through a podcast application form?
faq_plan.a: Listen to the first few minutes of one past interview, then read the pitch against your last 10 episodes to make sure it is not a repeat. For anyone you are unsure about, book a 15-minute call before the recording. With Emergent, every application lands in a database you own, where you can sort pitches by topic before deciding.

faq_plan.q: Can guests sign a recording release inside a podcast application form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can capture a typed or drawn signature on a release step at the end of the form. If you would rather not hold releases from people you turn down, show that step only after the host approves a guest. Have a lawyer review the release wording before it goes live, because the wording sets what the guest agrees to.

faq_plan.q: Can a podcast application form take sponsor inquiries too?
faq_plan.a: Keep them separate. A sponsor is a business offering a product, and its form reads more like a vendor application: the company, the product, the episodes they want, and a contact for invoicing. A second form keeps the host's queue about episodes while the sponsor requests go to whoever sells ad slots.

faq_plan.q: Can a podcast application form email guests after they apply?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can send each applicant an email the moment they submit, then another when the host marks them booked or declined. Write the decline message once, kindly and briefly, and let the status change send it. The app can also post a Slack alert to the host for each new application.

faq_plan.q: How do I track bookings from a podcast application form?
faq_plan.a: Give every application a status field such as New, Shortlisted, Booked, or Declined, plus the recording date once it is set. Ask Emergent for a dashboard that groups applications by status and shows the next 4 weeks of recordings. The form takes as many applications as come in, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How long should a podcast application form be?
faq_plan.a: Short enough to finish in about 5 minutes; for a guest, aim for 8 to 12 questions. Cut any question the host never reads before saying yes. The same test keeps a food bank application form short: every field there feeds a decision the pantry makes, and a podcast form should meet the same bar.
